ud1.9:0.2: The Discourse about Those with Knotted Hair
ud1.9:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Gayā, on Gayā Peak.
ud1.9:1.3: Then at that time many knotted-haired ascetics, in the cold Winter nights, in between ‘the eights’, at the time of the snowfall, in the Gayā (river), were plunging out, and plunging in, were plunging out and in,
ud1.9:1.4: were sprinkling (water), and were offering the fire sacrifice, (thinking): “Through this there is purity.”
ud1.9:2.1: The Fortunate One saw that those many knotted-haired ascetics, in the Winter nights, in between ‘the eights’, at the time of the snowfall, in the Gayā (river), were plunging out and plunging in, were plunging out and in,
ud1.9:2.2: were sprinkling (water), and were offering the fire sacrifice, (thinking): “Through this there is purity.”
ud1.9:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud1.9:4.1: “Not through water is there purity ~ - many people bathe here!
ud1.9:4.3: In whom there is truth and Dhamma,
ud1.9:4.4: ~ he is pure, and he is a brāhmaṇa.”
